entities.summary:
Chungmok, born Wang Hŭn, was the 29th king of the Goryeo Dynasty of Korea.

As the ruler from 1319 to 1349, Chungmok implemented various policies to strengthen the Goryeo economy and military.

His reign saw significant cultural achievements, including the production of a large number of Buddhist scriptures and the development of a unique Korean art style.

Chungmok's legacy extends beyond his own dynasty, as he played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism throughout Korea.

"We must not forget our ancestors," Chungmok once said, "for they have guided us to where we stand today."
